title: Systemic Error Swallowing via Blank Identifier and Relaxed Linter Configuration
summary: A census across production code identified 2,894 instances of the blank identifier `_ = `, with numerous occurrences directly discarding errors from critical operations including JSON unmarshaling (pkg/swarm/mcp_client.go:193, pkg/contextevents/json_codec.go:53), append-only kernel mutations (pkg/swarm/metabolism/exhaust.go:120, 153), file closes, and HTTP stream encoding (pkg/scheduler/handlers_callback_listener.go:367). This silent error suppression pattern is institutionalized in .golangci.yml, where errcheck explicitly sets check-blank: false and check-type-assertions: false, preventing static analysis tools from catching unhandled errors and panic-prone type assertions across the codebase.
recommendation: Re-enable check-blank: true and check-type-assertions: true in .golangci.yml. Audit all `_ = ` error discards in production code, replacing blind suppression with explicit error logging, error propagation, or explicit //nolint:errcheck justifications where operations are genuinely best-effort.
non_goals: Forbidding blank identifiers for genuinely unused variables in loop iterations
Failing builds on test teardown file deletions

evidence.detail: errcheck configuration disables blank identifier and type assertion checking
Silent discard of error returned by streamA.RecordKernelMutation
Silent discard of json.Unmarshal error on tool parameter schema
2,894 total instances of blank identifier _ = in non-test Go source files

citations.point: Do not discard errors with the blank identifier unless their failure is genuinely non-actionable; unhandled errors cause cascading silent failures.
Reliability and Fault Tolerance: Software must handle exceptions and errors without silently continuing in corrupted states.

title: Silent Failure Suppression via Checked nilerr Returns in CLI and System Daemons
summary: Static analysis using the nilerr analyzer uncovered over 50 instances in cmd/ where code explicitly checks if err != nil, yet returns nil or obj, nil instead of propagating or handling the error. Prominent examples include cmd/zqk/ambient/daemon.go:279 (swallowing stream reader errors), cmd/zqk/scheduler/scheduler_daemon.go:84 (swallowing status collection failures), cmd/zqk/object/update.go:439 (swallowing update validation failures), and cmd/zqk/system/async_check.go:1238. This anti-pattern leads to false-positive success states where operations fail silently without warning the caller or operator.
recommendation: Enable the nilerr linter in .golangci.yml. Refactor all flagged functions to return the captured err wrapped with contextual information, or explicitly log the warning at an appropriate severity level if intentional best-effort behavior is required.
non_goals: Preventing intentional graceful degradation where documented and logged
Changing CLI exit code semantics for non-fatal warnings

evidence.detail: Detected 50 instances of nilerr where err != nil checks return nil
Error is checked at line 275 but nil is returned at line 279
Status collection error checked at line 82 but nil returned at line 84
Error checked at line 437 but nil returned at line 439

citations.point: Never return a nil error when an error check has caught a non-nil failure condition; callers rely on error semantics to determine success.
Go error-handling idiom requires that if a function returns an error, callers can trust that nil indicates complete success.

title: Broken Error Wrapping Chains Using %v/%s Formatting Instead of %w
summary: Systematic inspection of error construction identified 50 instances where fmt.Errorf or errfmt.Errorf format an underlying error using %v or %s format verbs rather than the Go 1.13 %w wrapping verb. In critical modules such as cmd/zqk/app/auth_middleware.go:179 (unauthorized: storage not available to validate session: %v), cmd/zqk/system/git.go:169 (failed to query code references: %v), and cmd/zqk/object/demote.go:50 (failed to initialize spec loader: %v), formatting with %v destroys the error chain, making it impossible for upstream callers to inspect error types or sentinel errors with errors.Is() or errors.As().
recommendation: Replace all %v and %s format specifiers that format error instances with %w in fmt.Errorf and errfmt.Errorf invocations. Enable the errorlint linter in .golangci.yml to automatically prevent error chain severance across the codebase.
non_goals: Replacing sentinel error comparisons where errors are intentionally masked across public API boundaries

evidence.detail: Auth error wrapped with %v instead of %w, destroying error chain
Git code reference error wrapped with %v instead of %w
Spec loader initialization error formatted with %v instead of %w
50 production Go locations where format strings without %w receive an error variable

citations.point: The %w verb formats an error and provides an Unwrap method returning it. Using %v or %s severs the error chain and breaks errors.Is / errors.As.
Always use %w when adding context to an error that callers may want to programmatically inspect.

title: Magic File Permissions, Hardcoded Paths, and Proliferation of Duplicate Literals
summary: An automated repository audit using scripts/check-hardcoded-paths-and-perms-repo.sh detected 20,962 literal violations, comprising 20,709 repeated duplicate string literals, 199 magic file/directory permissions (e.g. 0644, 0755, 0600), and 54 raw path literals containing hardcoded .zqk references. For example, pkg/quality/cef_pack_builder.go:155, 167, 168 embeds raw strings .zqk/runs/code-eval-latest, .zqk/process/, and .zqk/audit/ instead of referencing centralized directory constants from pkg/paths. This widespread literal repetition introduces severe drift risk and breaks path/permission portability.
recommendation: Execute automated migration via ./scripts/check-hardcoded-paths-and-perms-repo.sh . --fix to replace raw permissions with paths.FilePerm* / paths.DirPerm* and raw .zqk paths with paths.ProjectDataDir references. Introduce domain-specific constants for repeated string literals occurring across multiple modules.
non_goals: Eliminating simple one-off string literals with no domain meaning or single usage

evidence.detail: Found 20962 violations (paths: 54, permissions: 199, duplicate literals: 20709)
Raw string literals .zqk/runs/code-eval-latest, .zqk/process/, .zqk/audit/ embedded directly in Go code
Raw path literals /repo/.zqk/cas/objects/ab/123 and .zqk/wal/log.wal

citations.point: Avoid Magic Numbers and Literals: Replace raw magic numbers and literals with named constants that express domain intent.
Constants should be used for values that have semantic meaning or are repeated across the codebase.

title: Hardcoded Canonical CLI Name Literals Violating Repository Hygiene Rules
summary: Execution of ./bin/zqk-vet -suite hygiene raised 4 high-priority verification errors in cmd/zqk/swarm/run.go (lines 388, 411, 443) and pkg/swarm/pack/manifest.go (line 338). User-facing instructions and process execution fallbacks hardcode the literal string zqk (e.g. zqk agent orchestrate, zqk agent status, zqk new swarm, and exe = zqk on line 418), bypassing the project brand abstraction and canonical invocation helpers (pkg/paths.CLIUsage, CLIInvocation, RewriteCanonicalCLIInvocations).
recommendation: Replace all hardcoded zqk invocation strings in cmd/zqk/swarm/run.go and pkg/swarm/pack/manifest.go with paths.CLIInvocation() or paths.RewriteCanonicalCLIInvocations(), and replace exe = zqk with paths.ExecutableName(). Ensure ./bin/zqk-vet -suite hygiene passes with zero errors.
non_goals: Renaming root binary packaging artifacts in release scripts

evidence.detail: RESULT: FAIL (4 errors: cmd/zqk/swarm/run.go:388, 411, 443; pkg/swarm/pack/manifest.go:338)
Hardcoded zqk agent orchestrate in stage-only mode instruction string

Hardcoded zqk agent status OR zqk ui in post-launch output
Hardcoded zqk new swarm, zqk pack seal, zqk run in manifest header template

citations.point: All user-facing CLI invocations must pass through paths.CLIInvocation or RewriteCanonicalCLIInvocations to support branded binary renames.
Avoid hardcoding executable names and relative environment paths that prevent multi-tenant or relocated execution.

title: Systematic Code Clones and Dual-Tree Redundancy in CLI Command Builders
summary: Structural duplication analysis and dupl scanning revealed severe code clone proliferation across the CLI builder layer. The codebase contains two competing directory trees for command builders: pkg/cli/bldr_cli_cmd_v1 (669 files) and pkg/cli/command_builders/bldr_cli_cmd_v1 (209 files). A direct file-level comparison identified 168 identical files duplicated between these trees. Furthermore, intra-package clone analysis revealed copy-paste duplicates such as supervise_command_builder.go vs mcp_supervise_command_builder.go and trigger_command_builder.go vs job_trigger_command_builder.go. This dual-tree architecture creates extreme maintainability debt, reviewer confusion, and codegen drift.
recommendation: Deprecate and delete the orphaned pkg/cli/command_builders/ directory tree. Re-point code generation tools (scripts/generate_command_builders.go) exclusively to pkg/cli/bldr_cli_cmd_v1. Consolidate intra-package clone variants into single parameterized command builder factories.
non_goals: Refactoring the underlying Cobra command builder abstraction

evidence.command: filecmp analysis between pkg/cli/bldr_cli_cmd_v1 and pkg/cli/command_builders/bldr_cli_cmd_v1
evidence.detail: Found 168 completely identical Go files across both trees
Detected 18 clone pairs including supervise_command_builder.go vs mcp_supervise_command_builder.go
Identical duplicate of mcp_supervise_command_builder.go lines 3-36

citations.point: Duplicated Code: If you see the same code structure in more than one place, the program will be that much better if you can find a way to unify it.
citations.locator: Chapter 3: Bad Smells in Code - Duplicated Code

citations.point: Duplication is the primary enemy of a well-designed system. It represents missed abstractions and multiplied maintenance costs.

title: Uncontrolled Panic Anti-Pattern in Library and Subsystem Initialization
summary: An AST audit detected 19 panic() invocations in non-test production Go library packages. Rather than returning descriptive errors to callers, packages panic during normal operational flows: pkg/mcp/permission_format_helpers.go:87 panics if object kind examples cannot be formatted; pkg/mcp/role_aware_prompts.go:270 panics if role guidance fails to generate; pkg/config/property.go:92 panics on a missing config property; and pkg/kernelcas/compose/evaluate.go:43, 154 panics if WarmDefaultRegistry returns an error. Crashing the process inside library packages breaks server resilience, corrupts daemon lifecycles, and violates Go error handling idioms.
recommendation: Eliminate all panic() calls in pkg/ library packages. Refactor constructors and evaluators to return (Result, error) tuples. Reserve panics exclusively for unrecoverable programmer invariant violations in application entrypoints or package init() functions where program execution is impossible.
non_goals: Removing t.Fatal or panic from test helper packages

evidence.detail: Panics during MCP server configuration rather than returning an error
Panics on role guidance generation failure
Panics on missing required configuration property
Panics on WarmDefaultRegistry initialization failure

citations.point: The standard way to report an error to a caller is to return an error as an extra return value. Do not use panic for normal execution or predictable error conditions.
Do not use panic for normal error handling. Reserve panic for truly unrecoverable errors, such as nil pointer dereferences or internal invariant breaches.

title: Detached Root Contexts and Un-cancellable Sleep Loops in Service Pipelines
summary: Auditing context propagation and concurrency hygiene identified 216 occurrences of detached context.Background() / context.TODO() in non-root pkg/ library packages, combined with 42 synchronous time.Sleep() calls in production packages. A prominent example is pkg/mcp/proxy.go:153-172, where connectionLoop invokes time.Sleep(1 * time.Second) unconditionally inside a loop without selecting on ctx.Done(). Furthermore, in pkg/mesh/webhook_listener.go:43, incoming HTTP webhook handlers invoke store.Update(context.Background(), ...) instead of binding the request context, severing cancellation propagation when clients disconnect or timeouts expire.
recommendation: Pass caller contexts through all library APIs and replace detached context.Background() calls with parent contexts. In polling and retry loops, replace bare time.Sleep(d) with select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err(); case <-time.After(d): } to ensure instantaneous response to cancellation signals.
non_goals: Modifying CLI root commands where context.Background() is the legitimate top-level root

evidence.detail: connectionLoop blocks on time.Sleep(1 * time.Second) regardless of context cancellation
store.Update called with detached context.Background() inside HTTP webhook handler
216 occurrences of context.Background/TODO and 42 time.Sleep invocations across non-test pkg/ code

citations.point: Pass a Context as the first argument to functions that do I/O or long-running work. Never create a context.Background() in a function that already receives or can inherit a context.
Contexts should flow through the program from top to bottom. Do not use context.Background() inside request-handling or worker functions.

title: Orphaned Uncompilable Test Source Causing Package Build Failure in pkg/testing
summary: Verification of package test suites revealed that pkg/testing fails compilation during go test ./pkg/testing due to an undefined function reference in pkg/testing/package_timeouts_test.go:10. The test invokes GetMinTimeoutSecondsForPackage(dir, ...), a symbol that does not exist anywhere in the codebase. Because this test file belongs to package testing and is committed into the repository, running go test ./pkg/testing or static analysis with test compilation immediately fails with exit code 1 (FAIL github.com/zqk-os/zqk/pkg/testing [build failed]), indicating missing test hygiene gating in pre-commit workflows.
recommendation: Either implement the missing GetMinTimeoutSecondsForPackage helper in pkg/testing or remove the orphaned test file pkg/testing/package_timeouts_test.go. Add go test -run=^$ ./... (compile-only test verification) to pre-commit and CI verification workflows to fail closed on uncompilable test code.
non_goals: Refactoring other helper functions in pkg/testing

evidence.detail: pkg/testing/package_timeouts_test.go:10:12: undefined: GetMinTimeoutSecondsForPackage (build failed)
Test references non-existent GetMinTimeoutSecondsForPackage symbol

citations.point: All tests in the source tree must compile and pass cleanly; uncompilable or broken test files erode team confidence and block continuous integration.
Test-Driven Development and Continuous Verification: All test packages must build and pass deterministically.

title: Pervasive Exported Symbol Package Name Stutter Across Core Domain Packages
summary: An AST census identified 270 exported types and functions that repeat their enclosing package name as a prefix, a practice known as package stutter. Prominent examples include pkg/pipeline defining PipelineRouter, PipelinePlugin, and PipelineStorageProvider; pkg/swarm/metabolism defining MetabolismEngine; pkg/sentinel defining SentinelPayload; pkg/vitality defining VitalityMonitor; and pkg/contextevents defining ContextEventsJSONLPath. When imported by callers, these produce redundant stuttering identifiers such as pipeline.PipelineRouter and metabolism.MetabolismEngine, violating Go canonical naming philosophy and increasing cognitive burden during code review.
recommendation: Refactor stuttering exported symbols to idiomatic Go naming conventions (e.g. rename pipeline.PipelineRouter to pipeline.Router, metabolism.MetabolismEngine to metabolism.Engine, sentinel.SentinelPayload to sentinel.Payload). Provide deprecated aliases during transition if external package compatibility is required.
non_goals: Renaming unexported internal helper structs where package context is not part of the selector

evidence.detail: 270 stuttering exported symbols identified across pkg/ directory tree
package pipeline defines PipelineRouter instead of Router
package metabolism defines MetabolismEngine instead of Engine
package vitality defines VitalityMonitor instead of Monitor

citations.point: Package name is part of the selector: The package name is used to access its contents. Do not stutter: inside package bytes, the function is Compare, not BytesCompare.
Package vs. Symbol: Avoid stutter between the package name and the symbols it exports (e.g. use http.Client, not http.HttpClient).

title: Monolithic Package Sprawl and Single-File Complexity Outliers
summary: Structural analysis identified severe module sprawl and file size outliers that impair maintainability and reviewability. Several packages have exploded into monolithic god packages: pkg/cli/bldr_cli_cmd_v1 contains 669 Go files, pkg/storage contains 627 Go files, cmd/zqk/system contains 478 Go files, and pkg/scheduler contains 447 Go files. In parallel, single-file complexity outliers exceed 1,500 to 2,000 LOC without modular subdivision: cmd/zqk/ui/model.go (2,004 LOC), cmd/zqk/test/dashboard.go (1,893 LOC), cmd/zqk/ui/views.go (1,785 LOC), and cmd/zqk/object/inspect_tui.go (1,730 LOC). This massive density makes local reasoning difficult, slows IDE indexing, and increases merge conflict frequencies.
recommendation: Establish package size ceilings (e.g. max 100 files per package) and file size guidelines (e.g. max 800 LOC per file). Decompose oversized packages into cohesive subpackages (e.g. subdividing cmd/zqk/system by administrative domain, and modularizing TUI models in cmd/zqk/ui/).
non_goals: Arbitrarily splitting cohesive, small utility files solely to satisfy LOC limits

citations.point: Classes and source files should be small. The first rule of classes is that they should be small. The second rule is that they should be smaller than that.
Modularity: Degree to which a system or computer program is composed of discrete components such that a change to one component has minimal impact on other components.
